learning: Iteration 5 showed that wheel_radius 0.04 m hurts, so speed is not the limit. This race tests whether added yaw inertia damps the drift that pins max_error at the 0.06 m floor.
notes: Mass test on the iteration 4 layout: mass 0.8 to 1.0 kg with wheel_radius back at 0.03 m. Controller is identical to iteration 4 so only inertia changes.
rationale: Evidence: iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.08 m, kp 1.35, kd 0.25, ki 0.02, mass 0.8 kg, wheel_radius 0.03 m) is the best design at 58.5. Every run still ends off_track with max_error at the 0.06 m floor. Iteration 5 (wheel_radius 0.04 m, gains scaled by 0.75) fell to 41.4, and s-bend progress collapsed from 0.185 to 0.0625, so ground speed is not the lever. Iteration 2 (lighter, shorter body with y=0.07) also lost s-bend progress (0.163 to 0.119), which is confounded but points toward inertia helping rather than hurting. This iteration isolates mass: wheel_radius returns to 0.03 m and mass rises from 0.8 to 1.0 kg, which raises yaw inertia by about 25 percent with the body unchanged. Because the geometry matches iteration 4 except mass, the controller is kept exactly at iteration 4 values so the race isolates the mass change. Expected: max_error and steering_oscillation fall on the s-bend and slalom, with progress holding at or above 0.185. Risk: a slower turn response could reduce progress, and in that case the controller will not be changed.
